docs.title: virtufin-tui
docs.text:
virtufin-tui is the operator dashboard for the Virtufin platform. It connects to virtufin-api and renders the full control plane — workers, WebSocket connections, state store, live CloudEvents — in a single keyboard-driven screen.

See the getting started guide to install and run.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph TUI["virtufin-tui (your laptop)"]
        DA["Dashboard dispatcher"]
        subgraph ST["Shared DataPump"]
            W["WorkersStore"]
            C["ConnsStore"]
            E["EventsStore"]
        end
        DA --> ST

        subgraph PAGES["Per-page Screens"]
            WP["WorkersPage (1)"]
            EP["EventsPage (2)"]
            CP["ConnectionsPage (3)"]
        end
        WP --> W
        EP --> E
        CP --> C
    end

    subgraph BG["Background tasks"]
        P["Poller (2s interval)"]
        S["Subscriber (Gateway.Subscribe)"]
    end
    P --> W
    P --> C
    S --> E

    API["virtufin-api (cluster)<br/>Gateway.* RPCs<br/>State.* RPCs<br/>Pubsub.* RPCs<br/>(talks to Dapr pubsub + state)"]

    TUI -- "gRPC :5002" --> BG
    BG -- "gRPC :5002" --> API

docs.title: 1. App (src/virtufin_tui/app.py)
docs.text: The root App subclass. Holds a single TuiConfig, connects to the active context, and pushes the Dashboard dispatcher. Global keybindings: q quit, ? help, 1/2/3 switch page.

docs.title: 2. Dashboard dispatcher (src/virtufin_tui/screens/dashboard.py)
docs.text: A thin Screen wrapper. Owns the DataPump (poller + subscriber) and routes the 1/2/3/4 keybindings to the matching per-page Screen. Page state is remembered across context switches.

docs.title: 3. Data store (src/virtufin_tui/store.py)
docs.text:
Three reactive containers populated by the DataPump:

Store Source Refresh WorkersStore client.list_workers() 2 s polling ConnsStore client.list_connections() 2 s polling EventsStore Gateway.Subscribe server-streaming Push, unbounded → bounded via append, max 500 entries

Per-page Screens subscribe to their store and re-render on each update. The DataPump survives page switches; hot context switching stops the old pump, re-creates the gRPC channel, and starts a fresh pump.

docs.title: 4. Config loader (src/virtufin_tui/config.py)
docs.text: Reads contexts.toml from ~/.config/virtufin/tui/ (XDG-aware via $XDG_CONFIG_HOME). Applies VIRTUFIN_TUI_API_HOST/VIRTUFIN_TUI_API_PORT/ VIRTUFIN_TUI_CONTEXT env-var overrides. Returns a TuiConfig with the list of contexts and the active one.

docs.title: 5. Client wrapper (src/virtufin_tui/client.py)
docs.text: Thin async wrapper around virtufin.api.client.ApiClient that exposes the operations the TUI needs as plain async methods (no Textual dependencies). This is what the pages call for CRUD (set-tag, start, stop, delete, etc.).

docs.title: 6. Per-page Screens (src/virtufin_tui/screens/*.py)
docs.text:
Screen File Keybindings Workers page (1) workers_page.py r refresh, Enter detail, a action modal Events page (2) events_page.py space pause/resume, c clear, / filter Connections page (3) connections_page.py r refresh, Enter detail, a action modal Scripts page (4) scripts_page.py r run, s save, n new, arrow keys navigate Contexts picker contexts_picker.py Push via c

All per-page Screens are Screen subclasses (not modals). Detail popovers (WorkerDetail, ConnectionDetail) and the action modal are pushed on top of the active page. The service browser is pushed via b.

docs.title: Real-time updates
docs.text:
The TUI uses two real-time paths, both running inside the DataPump at the Dashboard level:

  1. Polling (state lists) — ListWorkers and ListConnections every 2 s (configurable). Each poll writes into WorkersStore / ConnsStore, which triggers a re-render in the active per-page Screen.

  2. Streaming (events) — Gateway.Subscribe(services, topics, event_types) is opened once at context connect and consumed in a background task. Events append to the EventsStore (bounded deque, max 500 entries). The Events page subscribes to the store and re-renders the RichLog on each append.

On context switch (c → picker), the old DataPump is stopped cleanly, the gRPC channel is replaced, and a new DataPump is started.

docs.title: Cancellation / reconnect
docs.text: gRPC channels are wrapped in grpc.aio.insecure_channel (or secure_channel if tls: true). The subscriber task retries with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 30s cap) on disconnect. Events are queued in the EventsStore and are not replayed on reconnect. The store persists across page switches and is cleared only on context switch.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. virtufin-tui is invoked (from uvx, pip install, or local).
  2. app.main() parses --config and --context flags.
  3. config.load_config() reads contexts.toml and applies env-var overrides.
  4. If no contexts configured, the TUI opens the contexts picker and prompts the user to add one. On save, the TUI restarts with the new active context.
  5. Otherwise, VirtufinTuiApp.on_mount() creates a TuiClient, connects to the API, pushes the Dashboard dispatcher, and starts the DataPump.
  6. The Dashboard pushes the default page (WorkersPage) via push_screen. Keybindings 1/2/3 switch pages.
  7. On q (quit), the TUI cancels background tasks, closes the gRPC channel, and exits 0.

docs.title: Contexts
docs.text:
virtufin-tui supports multiple virtufin-api endpoints ("contexts") so you can operate against dev, staging, and prod from the same session.

See getting-started.md for the contexts.toml schema and the XDG-aware file path.

docs.title: Switching
docs.text: Press c in the TUI to open the contexts picker. Highlight a context and press Enter to make it active. Switching closes the current gRPC channel and opens new ones; the dashboard refreshes within 1 second.

docs.title: Programmatic override
docs.text:
For one-off overrides without editing contexts.toml, set the env var VIRTUFIN_TUI_CONTEXT=name. The TUI starts with that context active, ignoring the file's active_context setting.

VIRTUFIN_TUI_API_HOST and VIRTUFIN_TUI_API_PORT override the host/port of the active context (useful for ad-hoc connections to a port-forwarded gRPC server).

docs.title: Per-context settings
docs.text: Field Purpose tls Use TLS for the gRPC channel, verified against the system CA roots. Required for endpoints behind a TLS-terminating ingress; recommended for any non-localhost endpoint. api_key Sent as x-api-key metadata on every call. Required when the endpoint enforces API-key auth (the cluster ingress does); keys are provisioned per user in the API's ApiAuth:Keys config. The file's 0600 mode protects the stored key. worker_api_host The address a worker (a separate process the WorkManager spawns — e.g. the WebSocketManagerController example — not this TUI) must dial for its own callback connection to the virtufin-api Gateway. Defaults to api_host when unset. Set this when the worker runs somewhere api_host isn't reachable from — e.g. api_host is a TLS-terminating ingress address reachable only from outside the cluster, but the worker runs inside the cluster and needs a plaintext, cluster-internal address such as api.virtufin.svc.cluster.local. worker_api_port Port for worker_api_host. Defaults to api_port when unset. default_worker_topic If set, the events panel auto-subscribes to this topic on context start. Defaults to subscribing to the topic from the currently-highlighted row. description Free-form label shown in the picker (e.g. "Production — last deploy 2026-07-05").

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text: The contexts picker writes back to contexts.toml on every change. The active_context line is updated. The file is created with mode 0600 on Linux and macOS (XDG default).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# Recommended: use uvx (no install needed)
uvx --from virtufin-tui virtufin-tui

# Or install via pip
pip install virtufin-tui
virtufin-tui

# Or install via uv into a project
uv add virtufin-tui

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
If no ~/.config/virtufin/tui/contexts.toml exists, the TUI opens the contexts picker and prompts you to add a virtufin-api endpoint. A copyable template lives at contexts.toml.example in the repo root. Example contexts.toml:

[[contexts]]
name = "local"
api_host = "localhost"
api_port = 5002
description = "Local dev virtufin-api"

[[contexts]]
name = "staging"
api_host = "staging.virtufin.com"
api_port = 5002
tls = true
description = "Staging cluster"
default_worker_topic = "workmanager.lifecycle"

[[contexts]]
name = "kubernetes"
api_host = "api.virtufin.com"
api_port = 443
tls = true
worker_api_host = "api.virtufin.svc.cluster.local"
worker_api_port = 5002
description = "k3s cluster via ingress; workers dial the in-cluster Service directly"

active_context = "local"

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description name string required Display name (must be unique within [[contexts]]) api_host string required Hostname of the virtufin-api gRPC endpoint api_port int (1-65535) required Port of the gRPC endpoint (typically 5002) tls bool false Use TLS for the gRPC channel worker_api_host string unset (falls back to api_host) Address a spawned worker process dials for its own Gateway callback; set for contexts where the worker runs somewhere api_host isn't reachable from (e.g. cluster-internal) worker_api_port int (1-65535) unset (falls back to api_port) Port for worker_api_host default_worker_topic string unset Subscribe to this topic on start (typically workmanager.lifecycle) description string "" Shown in the contexts picker

Environment variables override file values:

Env var Overrides VIRTUFIN_TUI_API_HOST api_host of the active context VIRTUFIN_TUI_API_PORT api_port of the active context VIRTUFIN_TUI_CONTEXT active_context

Config file location (XDG-aware via platformdirs):

OS Path Linux ~/.config/virtufin/tui/contexts.toml macOS ~/Library/Application Support/virtufin/tui/contexts.toml Windows %APPDATA%\virtufin\tui\contexts.toml

docs.title: Switch context inside the TUI
docs.text: Press c to open the contexts picker. Switching closes the current gRPC channel and opens new ones to the selected endpoint. The dashboard refreshes within 1 second of the switch.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
git clone https://gitea.haenerconsulting.com/virtufin/virtufin-tui
cd virtufin-tui
uv sync
uv run virtufin-tui --context local
uv run pytest tests/
uv run ruff check src/ tests/

See architecture.md for the data flow and keybindings.md for the full keybinding table.

docs.title: Keybindings
docs.text: The default virtufin-tui keybindings. Press ? in the TUI for the same table inline.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: Key Action ? Show help overlay q Quit r Force-refresh the current panel Tab Cycle focus between panels c Open the contexts picker 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 Focus workers / connections / events / scripts panel

docs.title: Workers panel
docs.text: Key Action Enter Open detail popover for highlighted row a Open the action modal on the highlighted row s Start worker x Stop worker d Delete worker (with confirmation)

docs.title: Worker detail popover
docs.text: Key Action e Edit a single env var t Edit a single tag (or bulk via modal) h View code change history (calls GetWorkerHistory) l Hot-reload code from local file or URL Escape Close the popover

docs.title: Connections panel
docs.text: Key Action Enter Open connection detail popover a Open action modal (connect, disconnect, send) m Open send-message modal

docs.title: Events panel
docs.text: Key Action Space Pause / resume the live event stream c Clear the events buffer / Filter events (substring on ce-type or source)

docs.title: Scripts panel
docs.text:
Key Action ↑ / ↓ / j / k Navigate script list r Run the highlighted script (subprocess, isolated) s Save the edited script (user scripts only) n New user script (from template in ~/.config/virtufin/tui/examples/) f7 Select all in the editor Ctrl+C / Cmd+C When editor is focused: copy selection (Textual native). When output log or script list is focused: copy the entire output log to clipboard. Ctrl+V / Cmd+V Paste in the editor (Textual native, terminal bracketed paste) Ctrl+X / Cmd+X Cut selection in the editor (Textual native)

Textual's binding chain checks the focused widget first, so Ctrl+C on the editor copies a selection (native TextArea) and on the output log copies the full buffer (ScriptsPage Screen-level binding). The Ctrl+Shift+C variant does not work on modern terminals because the kitty keyboard protocol drops the shift modifier for printable characters. q is the global app-quit key — Ctrl+C does not quit, it copies (or shows a "Press q to quit" hint when no input widget is focused).

docs.title: Contexts picker
docs.text: Key Action n New context e Edit highlighted context d Delete highlighted context Enter Set highlighted context as active

docs.title: Action modal
docs.text:
Key Action Tab / Shift+Tab Move between fields Enter Submit Escape Cancel

The action modal also has a 2-second "undo" grace period for tag changes: after Enter, the TUI shows a hint "Press Ctrl-Z to undo" for 2 seconds. Undoing calls SetTag(key, "") to clear the tag.
